title: ALP (alkaline phosphatase)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: ALP is an enzyme found in all body tissues, but in higher amounts in the liver, bile ducts and bones. The test on its own cannot tell which part of the body the ALP comes from.
context: ALP is normally higher in children and teenagers, whose bones are growing, and during pregnancy. A fatty meal before the test can raise it slightly, and some medicines raise or lower it.
aboveRange: Normal bone growth in children and teenagers
A fatty meal before the test, or certain medicines
belowRange: Low zinc or protein, or poor nutrition
Birth control pills or certain medicines
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
